comment: Dr Kochel is amazing! She is so kind and cares about her students and I learned so much in this class. There is 1 paper, a midterm, a final, and a group project you work on all semester.

Dr. Kochel's lab was pretty low effort. We mostly did literature reviews and group work. Groups were randomly assigned and switched around often. We did two reflections which kind of felt like busy work but if you put in at least some effort you should be golden.

Dr. Kochel has got to be one of the best professors at UR. Her Child Development class was super interesting and engaging. She has a compassionate late policy which allows all students to be able to turn the assigments in by a specific date towards the end of the semester which is really helpful. She truly cares about her students and it shows.

Although Dr. Kochel's classes are a lot of work, don't let that scare you away. She spread it out throughout the semester in order to set you up for success. Second time taking her and this class is awesome. TAKE HER
Very caring professor and listens to students. Not much difficult work but there is a decent amount of reading. Lectures are interesting and she makes it easy to understand.

Taking a class with Dr. Kochel is a must! She is so passionate about psychology and her lectures clearly reflect that. There is a lot of work to be completed but it is all genuinely engaging. As long as you stay on track with the readings and assignments, you will easily succeed in her class.
Amazing professor, super kind and really makes an effort to get to know her students, even in huge lectures
Very easy to take online - really easy reading quizzes and participation points - wish it was more engaging but easy A

My PSYCH 100 was a 60 person lecture so it could be an outlier but its still a very easy class. You don't need to read, you just need to take notes during class. The hardest part is doing lab reports every week for the lab section. Overall, very manageable course. Also, Dr. Kochel is very smart and super sweet.

I absolutely loved Dr. Kochel, her child development class is very interesting & engaging. She uses a wide variety of evaluations from tests, essays & group projects, to class discussions to give every student a chance to excel in the class. She really wants to get to know her students and see them succeed. The work load and exams are manageable.

Honestly can't imagine why anyone would rate her lower than a 5. Dr. Kochel truly is a great mentor and professor for all her 300 and 361 students. She's super easy going which makes her very approachable. She's not a hard grader at all. She really takes interest in what YOU'RE interested in so you get to individualize your research with her.

Not sure why some of her ratings are so low on here. I would expect that its people who did not get to know her as a professor. She cares SO MUCH about her students and is such a gem. Definitely take child development its a great class and I have learned so much (even though half of the material is on zoom now). Amazing person and amazing prof.

This was taught like it was a 300 level course. The multiple choice questions were completely unclear, they were so oddly specific no one would know them. There was no exam with an A test average. I say 5 for difficulty because the expectations of non-majors was ridiculous. Not even the study guides helped prepare for the exam. Overall, horrible.

Great class if you like psych. Expect a lab assignment a week. Lab taught by teaching fellows- some are good some are not as good. Lectures are sometimes boring but always interactive and collaborative even with 88 people in the auditorium. Tests are very straightforward with no tricks. Come to class and study and youll pass.
I had Dr. Kochel for the lecture (not lab) portion of intro to psychological studies. It was a typical lecture based class and all the tests were straight forward and 100% m/c.

Most uninteresting lectures in the University. 80+ people in the lecture... still didnt know people's names the last class of the semester. Labs are terrible and taught, graded poorly by student teaching assistants.
